text: The Bourke Award, presented by the Royal Society of Chemistry, is an annual prize available to academics from outside the UK. It was originally established by the Faraday Society under the name Bourke Lectures and is now known as the Bourke Award. The award provides £2000 to experts in physical chemistry or chemical physics to present their research in the UK and includes a commemorative medal. In 2020, the Bourke Award was merged with the Liversidge Award to form the Bourke-Liversidge Award.
